Created the Department of Homeland Security by merging 22 agencies, the largest federal reorganization since 1947. It brought border security, immigration enforcement, emergency management, transportation security, and infrastructure protection under one cabinet department.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 107-296](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/107/public/296){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 6 U.S.C. 101 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/6/101?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Established the department and its mission to prevent terrorist attacks and reduce vulnerability.
- Transferred the Coast Guard, Secret Service, Customs, FEMA, TSA, and the functions of the former Immigration and Naturalization Service.
- Created an intelligence analysis and infrastructure protection function, later reorganized.
- Amended in 2018 to create the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.

## Why it matters

It defined homeland security as a field distinct from defense and intelligence. The department is the civilian hub for cyber threat sharing under the [Cyber Info Sharing Act](cisa-2015.qmd), and its intelligence office joined the community later reorganized by [IRTPA](irtpa-2004.qmd).

## Current status

In force as amended.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Framework statute. Standing laws that create institutions or general procedures other laws and executive actions plug into, such as the National Security Act, the War Powers Resolution, IEEPA, and FISA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Built upon by.** [Cyber Info Sharing Act](cisa-2015.qmd).
- **Era.** After September 11 ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 6: Surveillance law](../study/units/surveillance.qmd) (further reading); [Unit 8: The military at home](../study/units/military-at-home.qmd) (further reading).
